references.text: God's covenant with Abraham to give the land to his descendants, which is the basis for the promise of return to the land.
The promise to Isaac regarding the land and numerous descendants, repeated in Deuteronomy 30:5.
God's promise to Jacob concerning the land given to Abraham and Isaac, and that his descendants will become numerous.
Moses reminds the people of the land the Lord swore to give their fathers, which is the same theme as in 30:5.
The contrast between God's joy in doing good to His people and His judgment, contextualizing the promise in 30:5.
Jeremiah's prophecy that God will gather the people from all nations and bring them back to their own land.
Ezekiel's prophecy that God will bring the people out from among the nations and lead them back to their own land.
The promise that the people shall dwell in the land given to their fathers forever.
Amos' prophecy about the restoration of Israel, that they shall be planted in their land and never again be uprooted.
